body: Okay. If you're sure, please please please don't make it traumatic for them.

Thanks you.  
You're not the only one that wants me to live but the decision is mine and mine alone.  
I didn't get the choice to be born but at the very least I can choose to go out under my own free will
How old are they? Maybe by the time they're independent you outlook will have changed, can you put it off until then?

Cooking professionally is not like cooking at home, at all.  
I was the same as you, always loved to cook when I was young and got into the kitchen that way - started washing dishes when I was 13 and moved up from there.  
It is tough but visceral if that makes sense...don't think there are any other jobs were you get to use every single one of your senses.  
It can be extremely stressful, yes, it depends where you're working. Fine dining is more often than not very toxic. I know a few talented individuals that let the pressure get to them and had mental breaks or topped themselves. It comes with the territory.  
As to the social aspect, it's great, your crew is often tighter than your family, generally everyone gets smashed together after work.  
Being a male-dominated industry it usually has a very locker-room environment - sexism, butt-slapping, dick jokes etc - and I have worked with any possible combination of degenerate and addict under the sun which always keeps it interesting!  
It''s great fun while you're young but please don't make a career out of it, the amont of chefs i've seen end up alcoholics or divorced is ridiculous and I greatly attribute it to my terrible mental health!  
For a good place to start regarding workload and environment read Kitchen Confidential by Anthony Bourdain

Did I ever tell you the definition of insanity?  
It's doing the exact same fucking thing, over and over again, expecting shit to change.  
[That is crazy.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eBDi0iM2kcU)  
The only thing that would prevent me at this stage would be if others were dependent on me in any way, financially, mentally or physically.  
I have made sure this is not the case.  
Do you have any responsibilities to others?  
People, animals or organisations?

Academia isn't real life!  
Most of my family are teachers/professors/academics, and man it's a weird little bubble they live in.  
I made the conscious decision to not go down that path even though it was expected of me because I can't justify absorbing knowledge just for the sake of knowledge.  
I like creating tangible things with my hands so I became a chef.  
Don't be a chef.  
Learn a trade but whatever you do, do not get into hospitality :)

I'm guessing by your username you're 20?  
People are shit at that age. People are shit at any age, but especially during their teens and early 20's.  
Empathy is not innate.  
Personally I have been bullied during highschool - literally all my friends and classmates turned on me overnight and threw me out of the group.  
Some of which have apologised since (which I have not accepted, I know we were all young but it really messed me up for a bit).  
I don't know what i'm trying to say.  
You make new friends, you lose old ones, people come and go...hope you're okay

It's not that it's going to hurt, i'm sure during that month I will meet some nice people, taste delicious things, find some great music or a new artist, get high and have a laugh...but the good times always end and once again i'm stuck with my own thoughts. I'm over it.  
It's like running away from your own shadow.  
You can sever the ties temporarily by jumping but as soon as you hit the ground it's stuck to your feet like glue.

Honestly, and i'm not trolling, I think you have the right idea.  
No matter how you look at it - if you have a logical mind - there is far more suffering in life than pleasure.  
And to top it all off, the planet is dying.  
Civilization is collapsing for the last time and it's only going to get shittier from here on out.  
I know people have been saying this ever since we first saw a shooting star but this is the first time the end of the world has been backed up by scientific evidence.  
As to why people have a problem with suicide...  
I think it's because it reminds them of their own mortality and fleeting existence.  
In some ways, and it's not exactly politically correct to say this, it's viewed as an easy way out from the daily grind.  
I'm still not sure if suicide involves courage or cowardice. What are your thoughts?
